name: Eugene Dennis
bio: Eugene Dennis was the general secretary of the Communist Party USA and one of the original eleven party leaders convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial of conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the government. He was released from Atlanta around March 1, 1955 after serving about 40 months, then immediately re-arrested under the Smith Act's membership clause and freed on $5,000 bail.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government (1949); re-arrested 1955 under the membership clause
convicted: Convicted 1949; released March 1955; re-arrested under the membership clause
sentence: Five years; served ~40 months, then re-arrested in 1955

name: John Gates
bio: John Gates was the editor of the Daily Worker and one of the eleven Communist Party leaders convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial. He was released from Atlanta around March 1, 1955 after serving about 40 months and was at once re-arrested under the Smith Act's membership clause, then freed on $5,000 bail.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government (1949); re-arrested 1955 under the membership clause
convicted: Convicted 1949; released March 1955; re-arrested under the membership clause
sentence: Five years; served ~40 months, then re-arrested in 1955

name: Henry Winston
bio: Henry Winston was a Black Communist Party organizational secretary and one of the eleven leaders convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial. Rather than surrender for sentencing he went underground as a 'Smith Act refugee'; he surrendered in 1956 and later went blind in prison through medical neglect.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government (1949)
convicted: Convicted 1949; a fugitive from sentencing as of 1955
sentence: Five years (plus added time for jumping bail)

name: Gilbert Green
bio: Gilbert Green was a Communist Party leader from Chicago and one of the eleven convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial. He did not appear for sentencing and remained a 'Smith Act refugee' underground through 1955, surrendering in 1956.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government (1949)
convicted: Convicted 1949; a fugitive from sentencing as of 1955
sentence: Five years (plus added time for jumping bail)

name: Gus Hall
bio: Gus Hall was a Communist Party leader and one of the eleven convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial. He fled rather than begin his sentence, was captured, and by 1955 was imprisoned at Leavenworth with release set for 1958; he later became the party's long-time general secretary.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government (1949)
sentence: Five years plus added time; held at Leavenworth (release set 1958)

name: Robert Thompson
bio: Robert Thompson was a Communist Party leader and a decorated World War II combat veteran (Distinguished Service Cross) who was one of the eleven convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial. He fled, was recaptured, and was imprisoned; in 1955 the Veterans Administration moved to strip his disability pension because of the conviction.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government (1949)
sentence: Five years plus added time; assaulted in prison; pension revoked

name: Benjamin J. Davis
bio: Benjamin J. Davis was a Black Communist and former New York City councilman, one of the eleven convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial. Released from Terre Haute on March 1, 1955 after about 40 months, he was taken straight to a Pittsburgh jail to serve a 60-day contempt sentence for refusing to name names as a witness in the Pittsburgh Smith Act trial.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy (1949); then contempt of court for refusing to name names
convicted: Convicted 1949; released March 1955; jailed again for contempt
sentence: Five years; then 60 days for contempt

name: Jack Stachel
bio: Jack Stachel was a Communist Party leader and one of the eleven convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial. He was released from Danbury around March 1, 1955 after serving about 40 months, then re-arrested under the Smith Act's membership clause and freed on $5,000 bail.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government (1949); re-arrested 1955 under the membership clause
convicted: Convicted 1949; released March 1955; re-arrested under the membership clause
sentence: Five years; served ~40 months, then re-arrested in 1955

name: John Williamson
bio: John Williamson was the Communist Party's labor secretary and one of the eleven convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial. Scottish-born, he was released from Danbury around March 1, 1955 after about 40 months, then re-arrested under the membership clause and ultimately deported to Britain.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government (1949); re-arrested 1955 under the membership clause
convicted: Convicted 1949; released March 1955; re-arrested and faced deportation
sentence: Five years; served ~40 months, then re-arrested in 1955

name: Carl Winter
bio: Carl Winter was the Michigan Communist Party leader and one of the eleven convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial. He was released from Leavenworth around March 1, 1955 after about 40 months, then re-arrested under the Smith Act's membership clause and freed on $5,000 bail.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government (1949); re-arrested 1955 under the membership clause
convicted: Convicted 1949; released March 1955; re-arrested under the membership clause
sentence: Five years; served ~40 months, then re-arrested in 1955

name: Irving Potash
bio: Irving Potash was a furriers' union leader and one of the eleven Communist Party figures convicted in the 1949 Foley Square Smith Act trial. Russian-born, he was released in 1954 and, after Poland agreed to accept him, was deported there on February 25, 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government (1949); then deportation
convicted: Convicted 1949; released 1954; deported to Poland February 1955

name: William Z. Foster
bio: William Z. Foster was the national chairman of the Communist Party USA and the lead-named defendant in the 1948 Smith Act indictment of the party's leadership. His case was severed because of a serious heart condition and he was never brought to trial, but he remained under indictment through the 1950s.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
convicted: Indicted 1948; case severed for ill health; never tried
